summary: Cross-cutting conventions for doodleui-react. Apply these patterns consistently rather than treating each component in isolation.

animation.title: Animation (`animate` prop)
animation.summary: Sketch strokes draw in on mount and re-ink on interaction. Animation is on by default and opt-out.
rules: Wrap the tree in <DoodleUIProvider> once. Per-component `animate` wins when set.
`animate` defaults to true via the provider; pass `animate={false}` for a static sketch.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables animation unless the provider sets `forceAnimate`.
Per-component `animate={false}` still wins and forces a static sketch even with forceAnimate.
`animate` alone cannot override reduced motion; only `forceAnimate` on the provider can.
animation.example:
import { DoodleUIProvider, Button, Card } from "doodleui-react";

<DoodleUIProvider>
  <Button>Draws in</Button>
  <Card animate={false}>Static sketch</Card>
</DoodleUIProvider>

controlled-uncontrolled.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
controlled-uncontrolled.summary: Most interactive components support both modes, matching Radix prop names. Pass either the controlled pair or the default* prop — not both as active sources of truth.

asChild.title: asChild composition
asChild.summary: Many components accept `asChild` to merge props onto a single child via Radix Slot instead of rendering their default element.
rules: `asChild` defaults to false.
Pass a single React element child when using asChild.
Useful for rendering a Button as a Link, or Card as a section.

compound.title: Compound components
compound.summary: Compound components expose sub-parts via both Object.assign dot notation and named exports.
rules: Prefer compound parts over deprecated flat props (e.g. Card.Header over Card title=).
Dot notation: <Card.Header>, <Card.Title>, <Card.Content>, <Card.Footer>.
Named exports also work: CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent, CardFooter.
Parts must be used inside their root (e.g. Dialog parts inside <Dialog>).

forms.title: Form integration
forms.summary: Form controls work with native HTML forms, FormData, and react-hook-form.
rules: Input, Textarea, NativeSelect, and Radix-backed controls forward name, required, disabled, pattern, minLength, maxLength, min, max where applicable.
Use react-hook-form register() for native elements: Input, Textarea, NativeSelect.
Use Controller for Radix button-based controls: Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Select.
Set invalid / error / errorMessage for validation styling; stroke uses --doodle-ui-color-error and aria-invalid is set.
Prefer composing with Field for label + description + error wiring across a control.
Refs are forwarded on form controls for register() and focus management.

ssr.title: SSR & seed locking
ssr.summary: Sketch seeds and theme detection must be deterministic on the server and on the client's first hydration render.
rules: Never call Math.random() during render or useState initializers that affect SSR markup.
Use DEFAULT_SEED (0) for the first pass, then randomize in useEffect when uncontrolled.
Pass seed={42} (or any fixed number) to lock wobble for screenshots / Chromatic.
SketchSeedProvider initialSeed locks seeds; Shuffle (useSketchSeed().shuffle) is post-mount.
Prefer useIsomorphicLayoutEffect over useLayoutEffect under Next.js SSR.
ssr.example:
<Card seed={42} title="Stable screenshot" />
<SketchSeedProvider initialSeed={100}>
  <Button>Locked seed tree</Button>
</SketchSeedProvider>

theming.title: Theming
theming.summary: Reskin via CSS custom properties and/or DoodleUIProvider. Do not invent prop names for global sketchiness — use --doodle-ui-roughness.
rules: Import "doodleui-react/styles.css" once at the app root.
Override --doodle-ui-* variables on :root or a scoped wrapper.
Per-component sketch props (roughness, sketchColor, …) override provider and CSS for that instance.
Library does not load Google Fonts — set --doodle-ui-font-family after adding a font.
